flawed_step: The claim that every finite unit-distance graph in the plane is 3-colorable is false.
counterexample: Moser spindle: A=(0,0), B=(√3/2,1/2), C=(√3/2,-1/2), D=(√3,0), and E,F,G = rotations of B,C,D by θ with cosθ=5/6, sinθ=√11/6 (G=(5√3/6,√33/6)). Unit distances: AB,AC,BC,BD,CD,AE,AF,EF,EG,FG, and DG (|DG|²=3[(1/6)²+11/36]=1). In any 3-coloring, triangle ABC uses all 3 colors and D (adjacent to B,C) must match A; likewise G must match A. Then D and G have the same color but are adjacent. Contradiction, so the chromatic number is ≥4.
assessment_summary: The Moser spindle is a 7-vertex unit-distance graph with no proper 3-coloring, so the first clause is false and the statement is INVALID.
